date.as_written: āṅgirā nāmasaṃvatsare kārtikemāse śukravāsare ʼṣṭamyāṃ tithau ... saṃvat 1920 || mi. kā. kṛ. 13 caṃ

notes: The colophon has two dates that conflict. (1) The scribe's own date: Āṅgiras saṃvatsara, Kārtika, Friday, aṣṭamī (the pakṣa is not stated; 'śukra' is the weekday, Friday). Āṅgiras is year 6 of the 60-year cycle, so in the southern reckoning used at Satara this is 1872 CE (ŚS 1794); 1812 CE is also possible. (2) 'saṃvat 1920 mi[ti] kā[rtika] kṛ[ṣṇa] 13 caṃ[dravāra]', a Monday. Read as VS this gives 1863 CE, which is not an Āṅgiras year. Read as ŚS it would be impossible. Line (2) follows a second ending ('iti ghaṭakarparaṭīkā samāptāḥ') on fol. 6r7–8 and is probably a later addition, perhaps a Nepalese VS note. The copying itself most likely dates to about 1872. 'śaṃkaraputra siddhivināyaka' is the deity Gaṇeśa, not a person. Mālavade and Sānayiti are upanāmas (family surnames). Satara is in Maharashtra.
